decisions.reason: Its weak visibility even at launch and disappearance thereafter suggest results fell below aspiration, so a German specialty-machinery firm would reallocate scarce engineering and service resources back to stronger core lines.

Although it had its own page at launch, its absence in later years indicates performance did not justify continued attention, and under below-aspiration results the firm would stop the line and redirect resources to core businesses or new search.

The product seems not to have built enough sustained market presence to meet aspiration levels, so with limited slack the firm would discontinue it and use the released capabilities in more promising established or developmental activities.

A truck-mounted variant adds complexity and support demands, and since it also vanished after launch the likely below-aspiration outcome would lead management to drop it rather than carry an uncertain niche product.
